findings.title: `canView()` ignores `MANAGE` permission and `canView(ClientModel)` bypasses negative client permissions
findings.body:
There are two permission evaluation bugs in `canView(ClientModel)` and `canView()`:

1. `canView()` (line 86) only checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` and does not check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (or `canManage()`), unlike `canView(ClientScopeModel)` at line 121 and `UserPermissionsV2.canView()`. If an admin is granted `MANAGE` permission on all clients (`Clients`), `canView()` returns `false`, causing `requireView()`, `canViewClientScopes()`, `requireViewClientScopes()`, `canList()`, `canListClientScopes()`, and `clients().findAll(true)` (`viewableOnly=true`) to fail.
2. `canView(ClientModel client)` (line 78) calls `canView()` before evaluating permissions on `client`. Because `canView()` evaluates the all-clients `Clients` resource first, if an admin has a positive `VIEW` permission on all clients and a `Logic.NEGATIVE` permission denying `VIEW` on a specific client (analogous to `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewUserPermission`), `canView()` returns `true` and `canView(client)` short-circuits to `true`, completely ignoring the negative permission on `client`.

In addition, `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` only checks a single scope even though `root.evaluatePermission` already evaluates all scopes on the resource, so `canView(client)` can trigger up to four separate policy evaluations (`canView()`, `canManage(client)`, `canConfigure(client)`, and `hasPermission(client, VIEW)`) instead of checking `VIEW`, `CONFIGURE`, and `MANAGE` in a single evaluation.

findings.title: `getClientsWithPermission` never matches individual client resources or implied scopes
findings.body:
`ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` looks up client resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However:

1. When `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104) creates a resource for a specific client, it never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. Only the all-clients resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` (with `name = "Clients"`) has `type = "Clients"`. As a result, `findByType` never finds any individual client resources and instead only matches the all-clients resource (adding the literal string `"Clients"` rather than client IDs).
2. `hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String)` (line 274) only checks exact scope equality (`scope.equals(s)`). When `ClientsResource.getClients` calls `auth.clients().getClientsWithPermission(ClientPermissionManagement.VIEW_SCOPE)` (for example, when `viewableOnly=true` via `clients().findAll(true)`), clients on which the caller was granted `manage` or `configure` permissions (which imply `view`) are not matched.

Consequently, `clients().findAll(true)` returns an empty list whenever a caller only has permissions (`view`, `configure`, or `manage`) on specific clients, or `manage` permission on all clients.

findings.title: `getResourceName` does not handle the `CLIENTS` resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` stores `client.getId()` (the internal UUID) as the resource name when creating a resource for the `Clients` resource type, just as it stores `user.getId()` for `Users`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only handles `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`) and was not updated for `CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType)` (to return `"All clients"` or `client.getClientId()`). As a result, converting policy resources to representations for `Clients` permissions returns raw client UUIDs (or `"Clients"`) instead of the client's `clientId`.

findings.title: Unused `getEvaluationContext` method, `logger` field, and imports in `ClientPermissionsV2`
findings.body: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (lines 262-272), `logger` (line 51), and the imports `Logger`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `Scope`, `EvaluationContext`, and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` are never used in `ClientPermissionsV2` (`getEvaluationContext` and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` were only used by `canExchangeTo` in V1 `ClientPermissions`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` in V2).
